fufu 0.18.0 adds `ff merge`, carries merge commits through every rewrite instead of refusing them, and lets a rewrite open the resolution session on a conflict in the same run. `ff diff` takes revisions, and `--fields` projects any verb's JSON.

## Merging

[`ff merge <branch>`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/merge/) takes a local or remote-tracking branch into the current one by a merge commit, or fast-forwards when the branch has nothing of its own. The base is refused with `merge/base`; `ff pull` and `ff restack` replay onto it. A conflicting auto-merge records a `merge` hold, exit 3, that [`ff resolve`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/resolve/) opens and [`ff done`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/done/) lands.

Every rewrite — restack, fold, done, absorb, lift, the cascade, and pull's remote axis — carries a merge in its range: its parents are re-merged and its own change applied on top. A merge left with one parent becomes an ordinary commit, reported under `flattened`. A merge that resolved a conflict keeps the resolution, and a conflict beneath it on either parent passes through to the session. The `rewrite/merge-in-range` refusal is gone. `ff resolve` on a branch whose commits already hold a merge of its base takes the base in by another merge commit.

`ff show`, `ff log -p`, and `ff diff -r` measure a merge against the auto-merge of its parents, so a clean merge is empty and a merge that resolved a conflict shows the resolution. JSON gains `against`.

## Resolving in the same run

`--resolve` on [`ff restack`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/restack/), [`ff pull`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/pull/), and `ff merge` opens the resolution session when the branch underfoot conflicts, exit 3 still. `fufu.onConflict` (`hold`, the default, or `resolve`) makes it standing and `--no-resolve` holds for one run. See [held rewrites](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/concepts/held-rewrites/).

`ff done` on a resolution whose fix uncovered the next conflict rolls the session to another round with the next conflict's markers in the working copy, exit 3 each round, and lands once a round leaves no conflict. One `ff undo` steps back a round. `ff done --abandon` closes the session and keeps the hold; `ff resolve --abandon` drops both.

A rewrite of a held branch no longer leaves the hold pointing at a base it lost: a re-aim with `ff restack --onto` or a fold of the source drops a held restack and says so, absorb, lift, describe, and done point the hold at the rewritten commit, and a held absorb, lift, done, or arrival refuses every rewrite with `held/already-held`.

## Diffs and views

[`ff diff`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/diff/) takes revisions: `-r <revset>` shows a connected set's whole patch, and `--from <rev>`/`--to <rev>` two points. A gapped, forked, or two-headed set is refused with `usage/revset-not-a-range`. A positional that names no path, such as `main..HEAD`, is refused with `usage/no-such-path` instead of printing an empty patch.

One view set on `ff diff`, [`ff show`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/show/), and [`ff log`](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/reference/cli/log/): `--stat`, `--name-only`, and `-U <n>`, with `ff log -p` hanging each row's patch under it and `ff show --no-patch` stopping at the message. `ff log --body` prints each row's message body, and `ff show` prints the message whole.

## Miscellaneous

- `--fields <list>` on every `--json` verb projects `data` to comma-separated dotted paths; a path that matches nothing is refused with `usage/no-such-field`. See [JSON output and scripting](https://tyler-johnson.github.io/fufu/agents/machine-surface/).
- `ff pull` on a branch holding a merge of its base leaves the branch alone and names it, rather than discarding the whole run.
- The `@` row of `ff status`, `ff log`, and `ff map` shows a multi-line pending description's subject only.
